newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Two top Mobutu generals surrender in Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Two top Mobutu generals surrender in Kinshasa.

text.p: The two most senior generals of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko still at large surrendered to Laurent Kabila's forces in Kinshasa on Wednesday in front of a crowd of jeering youths, witnesses said.

General Amela Lokima, military governor of Kinshasa and deputy armed forces chief of staff, and General Michel Elessi, commander of Mobutu's forces in the capital, turned up at a leading hotel and were taken away by security officials.
The two men, at one stage rumoured to have been killed by Mobutu loyalists angry that the armed forces were prepared to give up without a fight, were wearing civilian clothes.
They were among the more respected members of Mobutu's armed forces. It was not immediately clear where they had been hiding since the fall of the city.
Elessi was military governor of South Kivu province in eastern Zaire when it fell to Kabila's rebels, shortly after the start of the seven-month civil war.

The army's top general, Mahele Lieko Bokungo, was murdered in Kinshasa on Friday, the night before Kabila's rebels marched into the city. Diplomats say he was killed by a member or members of Mobutu's presidential guard.

Some said he had been due to meet Kabila to discuss the handover of power, following Friday's departure of Mobutu from the capital for his northern Zaire jungle palace. Mobutu himself later fled into exile. He was in Togo on Wednesday.
Soldiers from Mobutu's army have been handing themselves at army camps in Kinshasa since the weekend takeover of the city.
Some have re-enlisted with Kabila's forces. Some, particularly members of the once-feared presidential guard, have been detained. A presidential guard officer was summarily executed by rebel forces.
Kabila's forces have toured the city gathering weapons and stacking them at centralised collection points.
